title: TDL-1 — Tag Document Association Delivery
summary: project explicit Tag document identity into a complete private Tag-to-documents association
content_html:
TDL-1 — Tag Document Association Delivery

Status And Purpose

TDL-1 is complete. TDL-1.0 through TDL-1.3 shipped the first Tag-association delivery in Tag Document Linking, consuming the completed TDL-0 — Tag Document Metadata Authoring Refactor Delivery. The delivery establishes explicit document-owned Tag identity, a complete derived association, and the source-owned Tag-delete guard before Registry migration, primary selection, or Tag Semantic Tokens consume them.

Complete Outcome

The registered analysis/tags customisation accepts one optional scalar-string canonical tag_id alongside its existing group metadata. Missing identity remains an ordinary document state. Malformed identity is retained as non-blocking authoring evidence. Tag identity is never inferred from title, group, body, filename, route, selected row, neighbouring source, or Registry membership.

The TDL-0 Tag-document fields modal adds optional tag_id selection beside independently owned document group; Info displays both values read-only. Availability continues to derive from the configured assignable field declaration rather than a literal analysis/tags comparison. Edit metadata remains free of both fields.

A private deterministic tag_id -> documents[] association contains exact {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} targets for every valid declaration. Several documents may declare one Tag. Each list is sorted by ascending {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} and that exact-target order is part of the private association contract consumed by the Tag Editor and Semantic Tokens. Association membership follows document source; only editing or deleting a document may add or remove membership. Group filtering remains an independent presentation concern; publishability and publication remain ordinary document lifecycle decisions.

Saving or clearing a document tag_id, importing that declaration, or deleting the document feeds the exact sub-scope rebuild that replaces this derived association product. The document workflow does not write canonical Tag Registry membership. TDL-2 presents the generated records beside their canonical Tag row so the product reads as one Tag-to-documents list without creating two editable membership owners.

Studio New Tag now creates only the canonical Registry row with no document association. A document is created independently and may later associate itself by selecting that canonical tag_id; Studio does not create, find, or assign a document as part of Tag creation.

Private association identity does not depend on public availability. Each row may compose a current public-safe title and URL when one exists, but a missing public descriptor does not erase, rename, or replace its exact authoring target. Management and diagnosis therefore remain exact-target operations while downstream public links consume only the optional location descriptor.

TDL-1 produces membership and canonical-order evidence only. Tag Registry continues to own canonical Tag identity, group, aliases, and its current doc_url[] field until TDL-2 performs the bounded migration. TDL-2 makes the ordered derived association list a read-only Tag Editor input, owns the optional scalar primary_document override and selector, and adds the deterministic target projection and Tag Semantic Token family. The editor never gains document search, association mutation, or reordering authority.

Delivery Discipline

TDL-1 extends the existing Analysis Tags customisation, private sub-scope manifest, Analysis-only document-location projection, focused association builder, and Studio Tag-delete boundary. The shipped docs_document_subjects receipt and atomic-build pattern is a useful exact-target implementation reference, but Tag associations remain a separate focused product rather than a new subject kind, generic relationship graph, or generic referential-integrity framework. TDL-1 must not become a lifecycle synchronizer or public Tag runtime.

The accepted TDL-0 seam declares tag_fields(group) in the registered Analysis Tags definition. The server accepts exactly that declared field set through /docs/assign-field-group, while the focused modal and Info projection consume the exact collection's private configuration and manifest record. TDL-1 must extend the declaration, Analysis Tags metadata normalizer, private manifest projection, modal response contract, and passive Info fields together when adding tag_id; a client-only or loose optional-field addition is not compatible with the strict assignment boundary. Document group remains independent from both tag_id and Registry group.

TDL-1.0 — Confirm Scope And Delivery

  • [x] Sanity-check optional tag_id, the accepted TDL-0 Tag-document field contribution, read-only Info, private manifest projection, exact Tag associations, existing group behavior, document locations, targeted builds, and public isolation against current broad owners; resolve only contradictions that would change the result.
  • [x] Confirm the broad blast radius across Analysis Tags front matter, customisation validation/import, Manage manifests, focused association output, document locations, and the TDL-2 migration handoff.
  • [x] Confirm the deliverables: optional scalar Tag identity, configured Tag-owned assignment and read-only display, deterministic zero-to-many associations in stable ascending exact-target order, non-blocking malformed evidence, exact document targets, current location descriptors, a bounded read-only consumer shape for later Tag Editor display, focused verification, and concise durable owner updates.
  • [x] Stop for review if implementation requires inferred identity, Registry-owned membership reads as the new association source, a generic graph/query framework, automatic Tag-document creation, document lifecycle coupling, or another boundary excluded above.

Checkpoint: a concise sanity note confirms implementation fit, broad owners, blast radius, deliverables, risks, private/public boundary, TDL-2 handoff, and stop condition. Stop before implementation approval.

TDL-1.1 — Implement Tag Declarations And Associations

  • [x] Extend the accepted TDL-0 assignable Tag-document field group and focused modal with optional canonical tag_id selection while Info remains read-only and Edit metadata remains document-agnostic.
  • [x] Extend Analysis Tags source validation, import, read/write, and manifest projection with optional scalar-string tag_id while preserving existing group metadata independently.
  • [x] Project normalized none, valid, malformed, and currently unavailable Tag identity states without making them lifecycle blockers.
  • [x] Generate deterministic exact tag_id -> documents[] associations from valid document declarations, sort each list by ascending {scope, sub_scope, doc_id}, and compose current document-location descriptors without inferring identity or reading Registry membership as source truth.
  • [x] Ensure assignment, reassignment, clear, import, and document Delete rebuild the exact derived association product without reading or mutating canonical Tag Registry primary state; TDL-2 treats a removed selected identity as stale preference evidence.
  • [x] Preserve zero-to-many membership, stable exact target identity, targeted-build behavior, private association access, read-only downstream consumption, and public isolation.
  • [x] Expose sufficient bounded migration evidence for TDL-2 to compare legacy Registry links with the declared association result.

Checkpoint: focused customisation, import, manifest, association ordering, location, zero/many, targeted-build, lifecycle-independence, and public-isolation evidence passes. An independent code/diff review confirms document declarations own membership and canonical order, group remains separate, and Registry migration/primary selection remain TDL-2-owned. Stop before TDL-1.2.

TDL-1.1 evidence (2026-08-11): focused service, customisation, metadata, build, import, transfer, Studio workflow, route, and durable browser-module checks pass. The targeted analysis/tags build writes one private docs_tag_associations_v1 product for 249 documents with zero current declared associations and no public copy. The scoped diff review confirms source-only membership, independent group metadata, exact ordered targets, non-blocking malformed and unavailable states, Registry-only New Tag, and no TDL-2 primary or migration behavior. TDL-1.2 has not started.

TDL-1.2 — Protect Associated Documents From Tag Delete

  • [x] Update Studio Delete Tag preview to resolve the exact Tag and current canonical document declarations, then list every blocking {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} association with useful current presentation evidence.
  • [x] Disable or reject confirmation while any current association exists and direct the author to edit or delete those documents first; Studio must not clear tag_id, delete documents, or cascade another mutation.
  • [x] Revalidate the exact current declarations immediately before canonical Tag deletion so a stale browser list or generated association product cannot authorize an unsafe write.
  • [x] Base eligibility only on current document declarations; empty, current, or stale Registry primary_document state is neither an association nor a Tag-delete blocker.
  • [x] Preserve ordinary Tag deletion when no document declares that tag_id, including exact activity and generated Registry follow-through.

Checkpoint: focused zero/one/many association, current/stale primary irrelevance, stale preview, exact-target, blocked-write, unassociated-delete, no-cascade, and public-isolation evidence passes. An independent code/diff review confirms Studio owns Tag deletion but document declarations alone decide whether deletion is safe. Stop before TDL-1.3.

TDL-1.2 evidence (2026-08-11): focused source-resolution, Studio workflow, mutation, route, modal-module, and localhost API checks pass. Delete preview lists each current declaring document as an exact linked target, keeps confirmation disabled while loading or blocked, and enables ordinary deletion only after a clear preview. Apply resolves current source again, so a declaration added after preview blocks the write; removing all declarations allows the write. One/many, unpublished, malformed or absent identity, stale Registry doc_url[], no-cascade, and stable exact-target order are covered. The current Registry has no primary_document field, and the guard reads neither Registry document links nor the private generated association as authorization; future primary state therefore remains irrelevant by construction. TDL-1.3 has not started.

TDL-1.3 — Verify And Transfer

  • [x] Prove no identity, one identity, several documents per Tag, unknown canonical Tag, malformed identity, deleted document, unavailable location, unpublished document, configured modal assignment, read-only Info, and targeted rebuild preservation.
  • [x] Prove no identity is inferred from mutable presentation or current UI context, no association mutation changes Tag Registry or document lifecycle, and Tag deletion cannot invalidate a current document declaration.
  • [x] Run focused Python, browser-module where presentation changes, source-lint, generated-doc, search, public-isolation, and whitespace checks.
  • [x] Perform the independent final code/delivery review and transfer the accepted declaration, association, location, freshness, and failure contracts to TDL-2.

TDL-1.3 Closeout Note — 11 August 2026

Final evidence passes 117 focused Python tests across declaration normalization, metadata assignment, manifest and association generation, ordering, optional locations, targeted builds, import, transfer, Studio deletion, stale preview, and no-cascade behavior. The Docs Viewer sub-scope report, metadata Info, managed sub-scope route, Studio Tag route, and localhost Tag API smokes pass, as do all changed production Python and JavaScript lint, the targeted analysis/tags build, generated Studio documentation and search, public-isolation checks, and git diff --check.

The closeout matrix covers missing, one, several, malformed, currently unavailable, deleted, and unpublished document states without inferred identity or lifecycle coupling. The current 249 managed documents generate a stable private docs_tag_associations_v1 product with zero declared associations because the 246 legacy Registry document URLs remain unmigrated TDL-2 input. The final code and omission review confirms source front matter alone owns membership, the generated association owns canonical order, Studio revalidates source before Tag deletion, and no Registry primary, migration, document-pill, or Tag Semantic Token implementation was started.

The settled declaration, exact-target association, optional-location, deterministic-order, source-freshness, malformed/unavailable, and delete-integrity contracts are transferred to the feature overview and TDL-2. TDL-1 is marked done and retained as bounded delivery evidence.

Completion Evidence

  • analysis/tags accepts optional explicit canonical tag_id independently from group metadata.
  • The Tag-owned modal edits configured document fields while Info remains read-only and Edit metadata retains only common document fields.
  • The private association product preserves exact zero-to-many Tag-document membership, stable ascending exact-target order, and current location descriptors; later Studio consumers cannot mutate or reorder that membership.
  • Studio Tag deletion revalidates current document declarations, blocks and identifies every exact association, and never cascades into document source.
  • Missing, malformed, stale, unpublished, and unavailable relationships retain explicit bounded behavior without changing document lifecycle.
  • Registry identity, aliases, group, doc_url[], and primary policy retain their current owner until TDL-2 migration.
  • Public document payloads contain only ordinary published document content and locations; private association infrastructure remains local.
